evals.expected_output: Should use a Validator trait with impl per rule, composed into Vec<Box<dyn Validator>>. NOT an enum ValidatorKind with a match in a single validate() function.

assertions.name: validator_trait
assertions.description: Each validation rule (required, email, regex, range, etc.) is its own struct implementing a common Validator/Rule trait — NOT enum variants matched in a single function

assertions.name: composable_rules
assertions.description: Rules are collected into a Vec<Box<dyn Validator>> or similar, and applying them iterates the collection. NOT a hand-written sequence of if-checks.

assertions.name: each_rule_owns_params
assertions.description: Each rule type owns its own parameters (e.g., MaxLength has a max field, Regex has a pattern field) — NOT a shared config struct or parallel arrays

assertions.name: adding_rule_is_isolated

evals.prompt: I'm building a log processing system in Rust. It reads log lines from various sources (files, stdin, network sockets), parses them into structured records, applies a chain of processors (filter by severity, redact sensitive fields, enrich with geo-IP data, aggregate metrics, sample at a rate), and then ships the results to various destinations (write to file, send to Elasticsearch, push to Kafka, print to stdout). We currently have 3 sources, 5 processors, and 4 destinations, and all three dimensions will grow as we add integrations. Build the core framework for me.
evals.expected_output: Should have three separate trait hierarchies: Source, Processor, Sink — each extensible independently. NOT a god function that reads-parses-filters-ships with match arms for each variant.

assertions.name: three_trait_hierarchies
assertions.description: Three independent traits (Source/Reader, Processor/Transform, Sink/Writer or similar) — each representing one dimension of change. NOT one big enum or one monolithic pipeline function.

assertions.name: processors_as_pipeline
assertions.description: Processors are composed into a Vec<Box<dyn Processor>> pipeline, not a match statement or a single function with if-chains for each processor type

assertions.name: each_component_independent
assertions.description: Each source, processor, and sink is its own struct with its own config/params. Adding a new Kafka sink doesn't require touching the file sink or any processor.

assertions.name: no_god_function
assertions.description: The main pipeline orchestration is a small function that wires source → processors → sink, NOT a 100+ line function that does everything inline

evals.prompt: Build me a task scheduler in Rust for a CI/CD system. Tasks have different execution strategies — some run a shell command, some make HTTP requests, some run Docker containers, some execute Rust closures. Each task can have retry logic, timeout configuration, and dependencies on other tasks (task B waits for task A). The scheduler should run independent tasks in parallel. We'll definitely add more execution strategies (Kubernetes jobs, AWS Lambda invocations, SSH commands) as we integrate with more platforms. Implement the core types and scheduler.
evals.expected_output: Should have an Executor trait for strategies, proper task graph with dependency resolution, clean separation between scheduling logic and execution logic.

assertions.name: executor_trait
assertions.description: Execution strategies are behind a trait (Executor, Runner, TaskKind, or similar). ShellExecutor, HttpExecutor, DockerExecutor are each separate types implementing it — NOT an enum with match arms in a single execute() function.

assertions.name: executor_owns_config
assertions.description: Each executor type holds its own configuration (ShellExecutor has command/args, HttpExecutor has url/method/headers, DockerExecutor has image/env). NOT a shared TaskConfig with Option fields for every strategy.

assertions.name: scheduler_decoupled_from_executors
assertions.description: The scheduler/runner handles dependency resolution and parallelism WITHOUT knowing about specific executor types. It works with &dyn Executor or Box<dyn Executor>.

assertions.name: adding_executor_isolated
assertions.description: Adding KubernetesExecutor or LambdaExecutor requires ONLY a new struct + impl. The scheduler, dependency resolution, retry logic, and existing executors are untouched.
